title: Five things we learned from UCL: Man United in crisis, and Ballon d'Or winner is clear - CBS Sports
description: Manchester United lost 4-1 away against Como and things are getting serious for Michael Carrick
body:
Manchester United lost 4-1 away against Como and things are getting serious for Michael Carrick
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Another Champions League night is in the books, and Wednesday delivered some incredible action. Bayern Munich were held to a 2–2 draw by Arsenal at home in a thrilling encounter. Alphonso Davies and Eberechi Eze found the net in the first half before Harry Kane converted a penalty, only for Declan Rice to score the equalizer and secure a point for the Gunners. Earlier in the day, Como dominated Manchester United to claim a stunning 4–1 victory on home soil. It was a historic result for the Italian side, representing one of the biggest moments in the club's history. For Manchester United, however, it was a night to forget and potentially one of the lowest points of Michael Carrick's tenure. Galatasaray won 4-2 away at Lille, while Aston Villa convinced and won 3-1 against Viking. Elsewhere, Real Betis won their third game in a row against Feyenoord and Club Brugge also won 3-0 against Lens. After two defeats against Real Madrid and Brugge, Inter struggled again but at the end won 1-0 against Shakhtar Donetsk despite playing with 10 men in the last 25 minutes of the match played at San Siro. Real Madrid showcased a convincing victory at the Bernabeu against RB Leipzig, with goals scored by Kylian Mbappe, Yan Diomande, Bernardo Silva and Arda Guler. Here's what we learned from Wednesday's Champions League action.Michael Carrick has lost the dressing room The 4–1 defeat to Como at the Stadio Sinigaglia on Wednesday could well have marked the lowest point of Michael Carrick's tenure at Manchester United, with the Red Devils suffering a humiliating loss on Italian soil. After the defeat, there are now increasing rumors on the future of the English coach, who is now seriously risking his job. There is a feeling that the relationship between some of the key players of the dressing room and the coach is now broken, as the words of Bruno Fernandes might suggest. Here's what the Portuguese midfielder said after the match:"It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence. That's on the manager and staff to see, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with them [Como], the center back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to," he said.
Carrick didn't seem happy about what Fernandes said and in the post-match press conference he said: "We actually half-pressed, man-to-man in the second half and then ended up conceding a goal from that. It's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run and you don't run forward and you don't run back, you ain't going to win." The general feeling is that this is not going to end well. Harry Kane deserves the Ballon d'Or The English striker is the frontrunner to win the 2026 edition of the Ballon d'Or, as the reports suggest. The ceremony will take place on Monday and to get into the mood of the day Harry Kane has delivered another stunning performance against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena. One incredible assist for the goal scored by Alphonso Davies and then the penalty scored at the beginning of the second half. To put his numbers into context, Kane has scored four goals in three Champions League games and delivered two assists. He is arguably the most decisive player in European football right now, and if he goes on to win the Ballon d'Or, it would be thoroughly deserved.
Kylian Mbappe's numbers are underrated Speaking of numbers, Kylian Mbappe's are underrated right now. The French striker has scored 73 goals in 101 games played in the Champions League including Wednesday against RB Leipzig and he's started off well in the current season with Real Madrid, leading the Spanish team under Jose Mourinho. With 12 goals in 12 appearances this season, his numbers speak for themselves. However, he still needs to win more trophies with Real Madrid to cement his legacy in Spain and in Europe. The fact that PSG have won two Champions League titles in the two years since his departure from the French club will continue to follow him until he delivers major silverware in Madrid. Maybe this is the right season and on Sunday there is the biggest match in Spain as Real Madrid will meet Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou, marking the comeback of Jose Mourinho at their rival stadium. 
Como are among the best teams in UCL We need to take a minute and speak about Como. If you follow Serie A, this result against Manchester United shouldn't surprise you at all. Cesc Fabregas and his team are showing week after week to be one of the best teams around Europe and one of the most interesting projects in the game. Nico Paz, the Argentinian talent who signed permanently from Real Madrid in the summer, delivered a stunning brace against Manchester United, his first goals in the Champions League. Looking at his skills, this is just the beginning. For him and for the club. Stay tuned, Como are just getting started. 
Inter didn't convince Inter finally won their first Champions League game of the season after two defeats against Real Madrid and Club Brugge. However, the 1-0 win against Shakhtar Donetsk didn't convince at all, especially for their approach in the first half, a recurring issue this season for the Nerazzurri. Things improved ironically when Alessandro Bastoni was sent off for a double yellow and Inter had to play with 10, and when the legendary midfielder Henrikh Mkhitaryan came in and delivered an amazing assist for Carlos Augusto.

title: Warriors exploring trades for Kristaps Porziņģis, who is contemplating future amid health issues, per report - CBS Sports
description: The Warriors released a statement on Wednesday saying Porziņģis will not be around the team
body:
The Warriors released a statement on Wednesday saying Porziņģis will not be around the team

    5:13 pm ET

        The Golden State Warriors are exploring trade options for Kristaps Porziņģis amid his ongoing health issues related to a POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) diagnosis, per ESPN. Porziņģis is also reportedly "contemplating his future in basketball" as he continues to deal with health problems.The Warriors issued a statement later on Wednesday saying they did not anticipate Porziņģis being around the team in the immediate future, but declined to comment on the trade report. This all comes hours before Golden State's season opener against the Lakers on Wednesday night."In response to today's media report regarding Kristaps Porziņģis, we are not going to comment on trade speculation or reports regarding his health-related matter or future," the Warriors said. "As noted last week, conversations between the Warriors, Kristaps and his representatives will remain private. We are not anticipating Kristaps being around the team in the immediate future. We'll provide additional updates when available and appropriate." That comes one week after the Warriors said Porziņģis would be out indefinitely but "will be around the team." 
Porziņģis re-signed with the Warriors this summer on a two-year, $40 million contract that pays him $20 million this season and has a $3 million guarantee for 2027-28. Porziņģis arrived in Golden State at the trade deadline last year in a deal with the Hawks, but appeared in just 15 games for the Warriors, averaging 16.1 points and 5.3 rebounds in his short tenure in the Bay. Still, Golden State was hopeful that he could be a key contributor in 2026-27 and gave him a sizable contract this summer to provide some needed frontcourt depth. However, Porziņģis has continued to have health problems that have kept him off of the court, missing all of training camp and the preseason. Porziņģis and the Warriors both released statements last week offering a vague update on his status. Porziņģis said he was feeling better and hoped to be back playing again soon -- and also shot down some wild online rumors about his condition. The Warriors noted Porziņģis met with the front office and medical staff and would be back with the team but did not have a timetable for a potential return. 
This latest news indicates the Warriors may not see a path back to the basketball court for Porziņģis, or at the least that they have concerns about him being a reliable contributor for a team that needs all hands on deck to try and make a playoff run in the West. The question is what team would be willing to trade for Porziņģis and what Golden State may have to give up to move him given how much uncertainty there is regarding his future. The Porziņģis contract always seemed designed to allow the Warriors to move it, but looking to trade Porziņģis with his current health status makes it a tougher sell to potential trade partners. The Warriors spent this summer positioning themselves to have maximum flexibility next offseason, including working out an extension with Stephen Curry for less than the max that will give them plenty of options to go star-chasing in 2027. That means the Warriors cannot afford to take on a bad contract long-term in a Porziņģis deal. If long-term money isn't coming back, then assets have to go out to get a team to take on his deal (effectively an expiring) and send back a player who could be useful to the Warriors' rotation.

body:
The family of the Hall of Fame college basketball coach said in a statement that the progressive cognitive condition is affecting his "daily life"
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The family of Hall of Fame basketball coach Bob Huggins said in a statement on Wednesday that the former Cincinnati, Kansas State and West Virginia coach is living with a "progressive cognitive condition" that is affecting his memory and daily aspects of his life. Huggins, who is the all-time winningest head coach in Cincinnati basketball history, is set to be inducted into the school's Hall of Fame class this week."Bob is living with a progressive cognitive condition that has begun to affect his memory, and aspects of his daily life," Huggins' family said in a statement. "While the family has chosen to keep this matter private over the past several months, they believe this is an appropriate time to share the news with the many people who have supported Bob throughout his remarkable career, particularly as he prepares to be honored with induction into the University of Cincinnati's James P. Kelly Athletics Hall of Fame."
Huggins, 73, coached at Cincinnati from 1989 to 2005 and won 399 games with the school before coaching at Kansas State in 2006. After one season at Kansas State, Huggins took the West Virginia job and spent 16 seasons with the school, which included a Final Four appearance in 2010.Huggins initially resigned from his post at West Virginia and subsequently retired in 2023 after being arrested for driving under the influence of alcohol. However, months later, Huggins doubled down and claimed he never technically resigned from the school.
During his four-decade-long coaching career, Huggins won 934 games, including 345 during his time at West Virginia.

title: Kristaps Porziņģis trade destinations: Three viable moves the Warriors could make - CBS Sports
description: Porziņģis is out indefinitely and could walk away from the game, but the Warriors could still find a way to move
body:
Porziņģis is out indefinitely and could walk away from the game, but the Warriors could still find a way to move him
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There's no such thing as an untradable player in the NBA. As frequently as we call contracts immovable, it's worth remembering that Russell Westbrook once changed teams in all five seasons of a supermax contract. Proximity to retirement isn't necessarily an impediment either. In 2007, the Dallas Mavericks managed to sign-and-trade Keith Van Horn roughly eight months after he played his final NBA game because they needed some filler salary to complete their Jason Kidd blockbuster. If a team wants to trade a player badly enough, there's almost always a way to do so.Still, the Golden State Warriors are facing an uphill climb to move Kristaps Porziņģis, at least for now. On Wednesday, ESPN reported that the Warriors are exploring possible deals involving their high-profile center, but for a variety of reasons, he is an enormously tricky player to trade right now:Porziņģis has been dealing with POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) over the past two seasons, and is considering stepping away from basketball for good. At the very least, availability concerns mean he has no positive trade value as a player right now. Any team considering acquiring him would have to view any future on-court value as merely a bonus.When they re-signed Porziņģis this offseason, the Warriors gave him a $3 million guarantee for the 2027-28 season. This is by no means an enormous figure, but in the apron era, every cent counts. No team is going to be eager to pay Porziņģis $3 million not to play for them, making him a bit more cumbersome than a traditional expiring contract. Frankly, this was a bizarre own goal on Golden State's part. One potential path for Golden State's 2027 offseason is near-max cap space, and considering Porziņģis would have needed to pass a physical with another team in order to leave, it's just hard to imagine he had the leverage to demand any sort of 2027-28 guarantee. That is especially true considering the Warriors are paying him $20 million this season, far above the mid-level exceptions most other teams had to potentially offer him.By virtue of using the taxpayer mid-level exception on De'Anthony Melton, the Warriors are hard-capped at the second apron. They only have around $350,000 in room beneath it right now, meaning Golden State lacks the wiggle room to take on a bigger salary than Porziņģis without adding other players.A good chunk of the NBA is not eligible to be traded right now. Most 2026 free agents are not tradable until Dec. 15, with a handful having to wait until Jan. 15 instead. Porziņģis notably avoids that fate because the Warriors managed to sneak his deal in right before the beginning of free agency, allowing them to structure it as an extension that did not include a raise big enough to trigger a six-month trade restriction. He can be moved right now, but many other players who might factor into a deal like this, including seven of his teammates, cannot.
        
            
                Warriors exploring trades for Kristaps Porziņģis, who is contemplating future amid health issues, per report
                
                    Robby Kalland                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Put all of this together and you have an enormously inconvenient set of trade circumstances. The Warriors, with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody also sidelined, are starting the season with almost $90 million in salary sitting out due to injuries that preceded this season. Part of their motivation in exploring a Porziņģis trade would likely be to salvage this season. If they have to wait until Dec. 15 for the right combination of players to become tradable, it might be too late. At best, Porziņģis is essentially just matching money from a trade perspective. At worst, he's someone they'll have to attach something to in order to move.
So, are there any viable moves out there? A few come to mind.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Milwaukee BucksThe best version of Golden State's roster is pretty dependent on having centers that can shoot. As the Warriors learned with Jonathan Kuminga, pairing a third shaky 3-point shooter with Butler and Draymond Green tends to compromise their spacing. Green can play center when needed, but at this point shouldn't do so on a full-time basis. And while Al Horford is here, he's 40 and not equipped for a starter's workload. This was the theoretical purpose of the Porziņģis acquisition. Golden State needs tall people who can make 3s, especially now that Quinten Post is gone.The only starting-caliber shooting center available at what would probably be a reasonable price is Myles Turner. The Milwaukee Bucks signed him in a last-ditch effort to keep Giannis Antetokounmpo. It didn't work. Turner had a bad year and has three expensive seasons left on his contract. With Kel'El Ware needing minutes to potentially grow into Milwaukee's long-term center, swapping out Turner for a shorter Porziņģis contract and Moody (needed for money-matching purposes) makes plenty of sense. 
The Bucks don't even have to worry about Porziņģis' health knocking them into the relegation zone because they don't control their own first-round pick. A team like Milwaukee, with no short-term stakes, is the ideal landing spot for Porziņģis. If he can come back down the line, great, he'd be a nice backup. If they have to cut him, well, it's not as though they needed that wiggle room anyway.
There's one pretty substantial hiccup here, though, and it's the remaining years left on Turner's contract. Adding him more or less takes max-level cap space off the table for the Warriors next summer. The question then becomes, how valuable is that option, really? Nikola Jokić and Antetokounmpo are technically slated for unrestricted free agency... but does anyone really doubt that they'll re-sign with their current teams? Even if they don't, why would they pick the aging Warriors? Karl-Anthony Towns can opt out of his contract in New York, but he's made it clear he wants to be a Knick for life. Odds are, something gets done there. Difference-makers just don't change teams through free agency anymore.Besides, preserving that cap space means renouncing their rights on their own free agents. Maybe Green takes a discount to stay for sentimental reasons. Butler has never shown a willingness to do that. Adding Turner robs the Warriors of upside over the next few years, but it's not as though Golden State really had much of it to begin with. What's the goal here? Are they genuinely trying to win a title? Or just trying to allow Stephen Curry to retire with some dignity? If it's the latter, Turner makes sense.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Charlotte HornetsThe Hornets willingly took a step back this season by trading LaMelo Ball, and ever since, they've been perfectly willing to take on money when it suits them. They got three second-round picks to eat the Dorian Finney-Smith contract, for example, and are more than flexible enough to waive Porziņģis next offseason if needed. If anything, they might prefer to use his inflated cap number and partial guarantee to get more draft capital to take on another bigger contract down the line.
The Hornets are relatively light on high-end talent but stuffed with mid-sized contracts attached to playable NBA veterans. Royce O'Neale could help the Warriors. Grant Williams could help the Warriors. Grayson Allen could help the Warriors, though they already have quite a few shooting guards. If the name of the game here is just "turn salary that isn't playing for us into salary that could play for us," Charlotte is a pretty easy fit. Of the three, Williams has the only expiring deal, but O'Neale has the lowest cap figure.The Warriors have three tradable second-round picks. Is that enough to make a deal like this happen? Maybe, depending on who the Hornets are sending out. Charlotte might want to see how its rotation shakes out over the first few weeks before landing on who, if anyone, it would want to trade. First-round capital, even a swap, just doesn't make sense in a deal this small, so it's either seconds or bust.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New Orleans PelicansThe Pelicans are mostly a placeholder for the concept of using Porziņģis' salary plus draft picks to trade for a very good player. The Warriors have, at times, been linked to both Trey Murphy and Herb Jones. The Pelicans, having re-signed Saddiq Bey to a three-year extension, may elect to move one of their other wings to eventually give him a starting job. Jones, as a shaky shooter, is the worst fit of the two. Murphy, given his scoring and team-friendly contract, would cost far more. Golden State controls most of its own draft capital. The question is how much, if any, actually makes sense to give up in a win-now trade.
Murphy is a very valuable No. 3 option. The Warriors are emphatically not a No. 3 option away from any sort of meaningful winning. If this is the direction the Warriors want to take a Porziņģis trade, it probably has to come with some proof of concept. If Curry can keep Golden State in, say, the race for the top six for a month or two, and Butler looks close to a return, then maybe it makes sense to make a trade involving multiple first-round picks. In the more likely event that the Warriors are more of a Play-In team (or worse), those picks become precious.Curry is still a top-10 player when healthy. He missed half of last season and is nearing the end of his legendary career. Golden State has to balance the upside his mere presence creates with the reality that his window probably closed when Butler tore his ACL last season. Getting better while he's still a star-level player would be nice. This is still, functionally, a rebuilding team, and basically everything would have to go right to justify trading future for present here.

title: Giants name JJ McCarthy starting QB for Week 7 game against Texans - CBS Sports
description: McCarthy is set to make his first career start for Big Blue
body:
McCarthy is set to make his first career start for Big Blue
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:18 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Giants have apparently made a decision on who their starting quarterback will be for this weekend's game against the Houston Texans. The plan is for JJ McCarthy to get the start, with Jameis Winston backing him up. McCarthy, who was traded from Minnesota earlier this season, is in line to make his first career start for the Giants, who are currently sitting atop the NFC East division with a 3-2-1 record. 
The Giants initially turned to Winston after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury in Week 2. As he is known to do, Winston had both good and bad moments over the past five games. He played well enough, though, to post a 2-1-1 record as the Giants' starting quarterback. Winston struggled on this past Sunday, and he was replaced in the second half by McCarthy, who engineered three fourth-quarter scoring drives. The comeback fell short, however, as the Saints left New Jersey with a 34-27 win. 
"I thought Jameis has done a tremendous job, won us games, played well. As we go forward here, this is going to be our direction. We think it gives us some good options on offense,'' John Harbaugh told reporters.Harbaugh chose McCarthy, who has displayed flashes of the player that compelled Minnesota to take him with the 10th overall pick in the 2024 draft. Injuries and inconsistent play, however, prevented McCarthy from having more success with the Vikings, who are off to a 5-0 start this season with Kyler Murray at quarterback. "I think he's a strong, young quarterback, has some experience in the National Football League," Harbaugh said of McCarthy shortly after the Giants traded for him. "Obviously, was a very high draft pick, very talented player and is going to make us a stronger football team."    
In 12 career games, McCarthy has completed just 57.2% of his passes with more interceptions (13) than touchdown passes (12). He has five touchdowns on the ground and an impressive 5.1 yards-per-carry average. "I think the last couple weeks, they've (the players) had a chance to see him practice and they're pretty fired up about it,'' Harbaugh said on Wednesday.Sunday's game was a microcosm of McCarthy's career up to this point. Despite having an underwhelming stat sheet, he was nonetheless able to engineer several successful scoring drives that got the Giants back in the game. 
McCarthy will face a Texans team that is finding its rhythm after a slow start to the season. 
The Texans, after a 0-4 start, have won two straight games after they defeated the Jaguars on Sunday in London. While this season hasn't been their best, the Texans have talented players on defense, especially pass rusher Will Anderson, who leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks. While McCarthy's mobility may be an asset, his lack of experience running the Giants' offense could also hold the Giants back. Quarterback isn't the only position the Giants need to solidify.  They also need to figure out who the starting running back is after Cam Skattebo — the Giants' starter on paper — inexplicably received zero carries during Sunday's loss to the Saints. Harbaugh said afterward that he is waiting for one of his running backs to earn the job. That player will not be Najee Harris, who was released on Tuesday.

title: Lions' Sam LaPorta voices displeasure about contract situation - CBS Sports
description: LaPorta is not a happy camper right now
body:
LaPorta is not a happy camper right now
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Sam LaPorta is taking a unique approach in terms of his contract situation. Instead of keeping things in-house, LaPorta has chosen to publicly voice his displeasure. A former Pro Bowler, LaPorta is in the final year of his four-year, $9.47 million rookie contract. He is slated to earn $5.78 million in cash earnings this season. LaPorta, based on his comments, is clearly not happy that he has yet to receive a contract extension from the Lions. "I think the combination of like getting your heartstrings twisted, as well as the violent sport that we play, you know, it sucks and it's disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt," LaPorta said on Pardon My Take. "You know, like last year, whatever it was week nine, week 10. I break my f-----g back for the team, and then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're not showing the love. "Yeah, it sucks. I'm going to continue to be a pro, and you know, I just a lot of that to my agent, and he handles that great. ... So I'm going to continue to go do my thing and ball out. And in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's gonna be all good. Yeah, I'll get paid somewhere else. So whatever." 
As he alluded to, LaPorta will likely have a big payday this offseason, whether it's with the Lions or someone else. His current market value is a three-year, $45.1 million deal, according to Spotrac. A former second-round pick, LaPorta has been a valuable part of the Lions' offense since he was drafted back in 2023. He made the Pro Bowl as a rookie and has caught 213 passes and 23 touchdowns in 47 regular season games. During the Lions' 2023 playoff run, he caught 21 of 27 targets for 176 yards and a score. LaPorta has bounced back this season after a serious back injury sidelined him for the second half of the 2025 campaign. He's been especially good over the past two games; he caught eight passes for 84 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers in Week 5 and caught each of his five targets for 88 yards and a score during last week's win over the Cardinals. It's very possible that the Lions -- and other potential teams that might be interested in his services -- are turned off by his decision to be so vocal about his contract status, especially with the Lions getting ready for a big showdown against the rival Packers. 
Talent, however, usually tops anything else in the NFL. As long as LaPorta continues to produce, he will surely have a robust market if he becomes a free agent this offseason. He has certainly made it clear that he is comfortable with the prospect of becoming a free agent for the first time this offseason if he and the Lions do not come to terms on a long-term deal.

title: Chris Ballard's Colts tenure: How missed Matthew Stafford trade changed franchise - CBS Sports
description: Indianapolis was among Stafford's preferred destinations in 2021, but Ballard chose a different path and never so
body:
Indianapolis was among Stafford's preferred destinations in 2021, but Ballard chose a different path and never solved the franchise's quarterback problem
        
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    
            
    
        The Indianapolis Colts dismissed general manager Chris Ballard one day after losing 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. The Colts dropped to 2-4 with the loss.Ballard is the first head coach or front office executive to be fired during the 2026 NFL season. His nearly 10-year tenure as Colts general manager was hindered by an inability to find a long-term solution at quarterback after Andrew Luck's surprising retirement shortly before the 2019 regular season started. The Colts haven't made the playoffs since going 11-5 in 2020 with a 39-year-old Philip Rivers, who signed a one-year, $25 million deal in free agency. Rivers retired following a 27-24 wild-card playoff game loss to the Buffalo Bills, who lost to the Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC Championship Game. There's one bold move Ballard could have made in 2021 that would have ended the revolving door at quarterback that has plagued the Colts and changed the franchise's trajectory. The Detroit Lions were accommodating Matthew Stafford's trade request. The Colts were on Stafford's short list of teams, along with the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers. Stafford mentioned during a March 2025 episode of Jason and Travis Kelce's "New Heights" podcast that he searched for houses in Indianapolis on Zillow before his trade to the Rams. 
The Lions received a 2022 first-round pick, a 2023 first-round pick, a 2021 third-round pick and Jared Goff, who was thought to be a throw-in "bridge quarterback" because of his hefty contract, from the Rams for Stafford. After a rocky start in Detroit, Goff has proven to be the answer at quarterback, earning a four-year, $212 million contract extension, averaging $53 million per year in 2024. A Ballard offer the Lions couldn't refuse would probably have been somewhere between the actual Stafford acquisition cost and the two quarterback trades made the following year, in 2022, for Deshaun Watson and Russell Wilson.What would it have taken for the Colts to land Stafford?The Seattle Seahawks dealt Wilson and a 2022 fourth-round pick to the Denver Broncos for multiple players (tight end Noah Fant, defensive lineman Shelby Harris and quarterback Drew Lock), 2022 and 2023 first-round picks, 2022 and 2023 second-round picks, and a 2022 fifth-round pick in March 2022. The Washington Commanders reportedly offered the Seahawks three first-round picks, but Wilson's no-trade clause, which he waived for the Broncos, gave him control over his destination.Watson's trade from the Houston Texans to the Cleveland Browns followed shortly thereafter. The Browns received Watson and a 2024 sixth-round pick for 2022, 2023, and 2024 first-round picks, a 2022 fourth-round pick, a 2023 third-round pick and a 2024 fourth-round pick.
Perhaps, a trade based around Ballard giving up 2021 (21st overall), 2022 and 2023 first-round picks for Stafford would have gotten the deal done. The Rams didn't have a 2021 first-round pick because of a trade with the Jacksonville Jaguars for cornerback Jalen Ramsey during the middle of the 2020 season.Ballard subsequently demonstrated he could take big swings in an attempt to improve the Colts' roster. At last year's trade deadline, Ballard went all in on the 2025 season when the Colts were 7-2 by obtaining All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner from the New York Jets for a 2026 first-round pick, a 2027 first-round pick and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell. That type of aggressiveness by Ballard in 2021 to stabilize the most important position on a football team, quarterback, would have prevented the failed Carson Wentz experiment. Wentz was acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2021 third-round pick and a conditional 2022 second-round pick that became a 2022 first-round pick because his 2021 season offensive playtime reached 75%. He was reunited with Frank Reich, who coached the Colts from 2018 until nine games into the 2022 season. Reich was Wentz's offensive coordinator for Wentz's first two years in the NFL with the Eagles, 2016 and 2017.
The salary cap wouldn't have been an impediment to getting Stafford. He had two years remaining on his $43 million contract, earning $20 million in 2021 and $23 million in 2022. Wentz had four years for $98.4 million left on his deal before reworking his contract, where $5 million of his $25.4 million in 2021 compensation was moved to 2022 for additional contract security.The reunion was short-lived. Wentz's poor play down the stretch in 2021, particularly during the regular season finale against the 2-14 Jaguars, when the Colts controlled their own playoff destiny but failed to secure a postseason berth, led to his departure. Colts owner the late Jim Irsay called acquiring Wentz a mistake shortly after he was dealt along with a 2022 second round pick (47th overall) and a 2022 seventh round pick to the Commanders for a 2022 second round pick (42nd overall), a 2022 third round pick and a conditional 2023 third round pick in March 2022. The 2023 selection didn't upgrade to a 2023 second-round pick since Wentz didn't take at least 70% of Washington's offensive snaps in 2022.An aging Matt Ryan was acquired in March of 2022 for a third-round pick. The Colts anticipated Ryan being the quarterback for two years, as his contract was restructured with $12 million of his 2023 salary becoming fully guaranteed. Father Time caught up to a then 37-year-old Ryan in 2022. Instead of contending for a playoff berth, the Colts finished 4-12-1 in 2022. Ryan was released in March 2023. He made $36.7 million for his one-year stint in Indianapolis.
Reaching for Anthony Richardson with 2023's fourth overall pick wouldn't have occurred either. Richardson was a boom-or-bust quarterback prospect with a low floor and a high ceiling. The Colts were enticed by his great arm strength and tremendous athleticism, overlooking his raw, inexperienced nature. Richardson had 13 starts in his three years at Florida.The Colts hedged their bet on Richardson by signing Daniel Jones to a one-year, $14 million contract worth up to $17 million through incentives in March 2025. Going with Jones, who was benched by the New York Giants 10 games into the 2024 season before his request for a release was granted, at quarterback in 2025 was initially more of an indictment of Richardson than anything else.Jones was having a surprising career resurrection when he tore his right Achilles late in the 2025 season. A 7-1 start turned into a stunning collapse where the Colts finished with an 8-9 record. 
Jones was given the seldom-used transition tag for $37.8 million before quickly signing a two-year, $ 88 million contract worth up to $100 million through incentives, with $60 million in guarantees, of which $49.49 million was fully guaranteed at signing in March. He has struggled so much this season that a benching isn't out of the question.Why Stafford would have made the Colts a contender Stafford paid immediate dividends for the Rams. After going 10-6 and being eliminated in the divisional playoffs in 2020, the Rams won Super Bowl LVI. Stafford arguably had the best season of his career to that point. He completed 67.2% of his passes for 4,886 yards with 41 touchdowns and 17 interceptions to post a 102.9 passer rating. Stafford finished in the NFL's top 10 for touchdown passes, passing yards, passer rating, and completion percentage, ranking second, third, sixth and 10th, respectively. More importantly, Stafford elevated his play in the postseason. Stafford's 2021 season was subsequently topped in 2025 when he was named NFL MVP.There's no guarantee the Colts would have duplicated the Rams' success with Stafford in 2021. The Colts surely would have made the playoffs with the upgrade at quarterback and challenged the Titans, who were 12-5 in 2021, for the AFC South crown. After all, the Colts went 9-8 with Wentz and were 11-5 in 2020. It's conceivable that the two-game win regression from 2020 could have resulted in no drop off in wins or at least a one-game win increase with Stafford at quarterback. 
The 2021 Colts had a strong offensive line anchored by perennial All-Pro offensive guard Quenton Nelson. Running back Jonathan Taylor easily was the league's best running back, winning the rushing title by 552 yards while averaging 5.5 yards per carry. The 2021 first team All-Pro led the NFL with 2,171 yards from scrimmage (combined rushing and receiving yards), 1,811 rushing yards, 20 total touchdowns and 18 rushing touchdowns. The Colts had a good defense featuring All-Pros DeForest Buckner and Shaquille Leonard respectively at defensive tackle and off-ball linebacker.Presumably, Stafford would have gotten a deal comparable to the four-year, $160 million extension he signed in 2022 with the Colts. Quite frankly, Stafford didn't fully exploit his substantial contract leverage, considering the Rams had just won the Super Bowl. Instead, he made a conscious decision to leave money on the table in a team-friendly deal that tied him with Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott as the league's fourth-highest-paid player upon signing at $40 million per year. This led to a somewhat contentious relationship with the Rams due to Stafford's unhappiness with his contract.Nonetheless, Stafford should have given the Colts an extended window as a contending team. Stafford has consistently performed as a top-10 quarterback at worst since joining the Rams, and at an elite level for extended periods. The road to the Super Bowl in the AFC still would have gone through the Chiefs and Patrick Mahomes. NFL MVPs Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson, who have yet to get to the Super Bowl with the Bills and Baltimore Ravens would have also been standing in the Colts' way. Ultimately, Ballard's ability to find talent while consistently being near the back of the NFL Draft and in free agency would have determined the Colts' success. Undoubtedly, the Colts wouldn't have gone 38-46-1 over the 2021 through 2025 seasons without any playoff appearances if Stafford had been the quarterback.

title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Saquon Barkley to Seahawks among 10 moves that need to happen - CBS Sports
description: The closer the NFL calendar creeps to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, the clearer it becomes which teams are buying and which are selling. T
body:
The closer the NFL calendar creeps to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, the clearer it becomes which teams are buying and which are selling. Three weeks out, there is already a divide between contenders and pretenders, so playing the role of matchmaker provides a myriad of potential trade pairings.A sweep across the league shows how Super Bowl contenders with roster holes, like the Seattle Seahawks and their running back position, match perfectly with downtrodden teams that own tradeable veterans, like the Philadelphia Eagles and Indianapolis Colts.Sometimes the obvious trade proposals never come to fruition. But in a lot of cases, if it makes sense on paper, then it makes sense in practice. There are a number of reunions, like Khalil Mack's potential return to the Chicago Bears, that just feel right.Here are 10 of those trades that feel so fitting that it would be a shame if they did not go through.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Saquon Barkley to SeahawksThe Seattle Seahawks ought to have extreme seller's remorse as they field a bottom-tier rushing attack and watch Kenneth Walker III run wild in Kansas City. Much of their disappointing 3-3 start can be attributed to an offense that ranks second-worst in EPA per rush, which leads one to wonder how much they regret letting Walker go in free agency. He is very much the missing piece, and they will rely on Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price to fill that gap when they return from injured reserve. Neither is an established No. 1 running back, though, so Seattle would benefit from admitting it needs a high-caliber starter, then placing Charbonnet back in his more natural secondary role and allowing Price to develop as a rookie third option.They would have to pay a hefty price to pry Saquon Barkley away from Philadelphia because of his immense value and his giant cap hit, but with the Eagles poised to watch this season wither away in the wake of countless personnel losses, they should be willing to at least field calls on their superstar running back. Seattle is in as much of a win-now mode as any team in the league and thus is in a position to give up premium draft capital for a player who can help it return to the Super Bowl.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Josh Sweat to CowboysIf Jerry Jones cannot turn the Dallas Cowboys into a winning football team, he is at least going to go down swinging. The Joey Porter Jr. trade earlier this season was one big move, but the defense clearly needs more blockbuster additions in order to climb out of the depths. Since Jones addressed the back end of the unit with the Porter deal, it may be time to turn back toward the line of scrimmage and address, again, an edge rusher group that is still lost without Micah Parsons.While Arizona Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort said in August that he has "no interest" in trading Josh Sweat, there might not be a more obvious trade candidate on a team that is not built to contend for anything in 2026. Sweat denied any displeasure with his contract, but there was offseason smoke that he sought a restructured deal or a trade. He is an expensive veteran for a franchise attempting to build a young core and boasts the kind of perennial sack production and team contract control that a competitive team would pay a premium for. If the Cowboys moved a couple of draft picks to land Sweat, this would be a win-win.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jonathan Taylor to VikingsThe NFL's stingiest defense is to credit for the Minnesota Vikings' perfect start. The margins in those five victories were nail-bitingly slim, though, because the offense has only done just enough to capitalize on Brian Flores' coaching masterclass on the other side of the ball. The passing game is what it is. There is no in-season upgrading over Kyler Murray, and the wide receiver group will always be in good shape so long as Justin Jefferson is there. The main area that needs improvement and, more importantly, can be improved, is the rushing unit. Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason (once healthy) are a serviceable tandem, yet the attack has accounted for only three touchdowns and ranks in the bottom quartile in EPA per rush. An infusion of stardom would take this offense to another level and make the Vikings true Super Bowl contenders.Enter Jonathan Taylor. Whether the Indianapolis Colts would part with their best player just over two months after they signed him to a two-year contract extension (the third-largest deal for a running back in NFL history) is unknown, but with general manager Chris Ballard fired and coach Shane Steichen potentially on his way out the door, too, this franchise could be headed toward a tear-down. Teams will call about Taylor. Minnesota needs to make sure it is in the conversation.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Khalil Mack to BearsIf there is one trade that is most likely to be completed by the deadline, a Khalil Mack reunion in Chicago has to be at the top of the list. The pairing almost makes too much sense. The Bears need pass-rushing help. Mack remains productive in the latter years of his career, albeit not quite at the All-Pro level of his Chicago heyday. The Los Angeles Chargers are prime candidates to sell expiring contracts, considering their 0-6 record. Everything points to these teams working together to send Mack back to his old home.The lift Mack would provide for an offense-first team could be a difference maker that sparks a deep postseason run. Now that Caleb Williams is healthy again, the Bears have the potential to score at will. The defense lags behind just enough to warrant a splashy trade deadline move, and this one is just waiting to be completed.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Chris Godwin Jr. to SteelersThere is a wide receiver injury crisis in Pittsburgh. Aaron Rodgers was on a hot streak until health issues depleted his supporting cast. In order to maximize the supposed last year of his career and stay in contention for the AFC North crown, the Steelers need to plug some immediate help into Rodgers' receiving room. 
Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are on injured reserve, and Ben Skowronek has a calf issue. It is up to DK Metcalf, rookie Germie Bernard and a couple of practice squad elevations to keep the passing game afloat.All of that makes the Steelers potentially desperate buyers at the deadline. Chris Godwin Jr. should be on their radar. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers, whom they just defeated in overtime, are drifting further into the abyss and should be ready to sell. His three-year contract makes him an expensive asset who struggles to stay on the field, and that is a profile that the Buccaneers would seemingly want to part with. He is healthy now, though, and that is what matters to the Steelers. Plus, he should be a tremendous fit next to Metcalf. Godwin spent every year prior to this one on the other side of a towering No. 1 target in Mike Evans, so he would be right at home in the same lineup as a similarly sizable go-to weapon like Metcalf.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Budda Baker to BillsThe Buffalo Bills are winning games in one way and one way only: Scoring a boatload of points. They have to. The defense is a sieve, specifically in the back end. No matter how much pressure Greg Rousseau and the front provide, opponents are able to pick apart the pass defense to the tune of 285.8 yards per game — the second most in the league. The slot defensive back spot is the biggest weakness, and there is an obvious upgrade potentially sitting on the trade market in Cardinals safety Budda Baker.Baker is versatile enough to play nickel or fall back deeper into coverage and would immediately be the best player in the Buffalo defensive backfield. He is the Cardinals' highest-paid player and remains under contract through 2027, but he carries a dead cap hit of only $3 million for next year, so moving on from him would not put Arizona in a long-term financial bind. That is an attractive proposition for a rebuilding team.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jauan Jennings to 49ersJauan Jennings was in a 49ers uniform less than a year ago and would be a perfect fit back in one this season. He led all San Francisco wide receivers in catches and yards in 2024 and 2025 and knows the Kyle Shanahan offense front and back, so with the 49ers fighting through a litany of wideout injuries, why not reunite with someone who can slot right back into the lineup and deliver difference-making plays from Day 1? 
The primary reason he is not on the squad right now is that the 49ers did not want to pay him long-term money, but the Minnesota Vikings did not either, so San Francisco can have him back on an expiring $8 million deal.Minnesota is clearly a horrible fit for Jennings, as he has been invisible in the offense with only five targets, two catches and 9 yards on the year. He is not part of the Vikings' plan, so they might as well get something in return for him before he inevitably walks away at the end of the season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jerry Jeudy to ChiefsHis usage is up over the last two weeks, but Jerry Jeudy still ranks only fifth on the Cleveland Browns in targets as the team prioritizes its exciting rookie tandem of KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston over the 27-year-old veteran. It appears as though he is being phased out of the offense. Coming off his best showing of the year — a four-catch, 69-yard effort — the time to move on from him is now.
The Kansas City Chiefs would be the perfect destination for Jeudy and are as needy at the wide receiver position as any team in the league. Not only could the former Pro Bowler carve out a top-three role in a receiving corps that lacks any reliability outside of Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy, but his transition to a new offense would be smoothed by the fact that wide receivers coach Chad O'Shea was the same wide receivers coach who oversaw his Pro Bowl campaign in Cleveland in 2024. Patrick Mahomes could use a gifted route-runner to go with his speedy weapons in Rice and Worthy, especially as this team barrels toward a potential Super Bowl run.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Riq Woolen to LionsThe defensive backfield situation in Detroit is bleak, and that might be putting it nicely. The NFL's worst pass defense is desperate for help at each secondary position, while Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph remain out with injuries at safety, and the cornerback unit still has not recovered from the loss of Terrion Arnold. Since the Lions keep scoring at an elite level and own plenty of pieces on the rest of the defense, there might not be a more glaring missing link for a postseason contender than their secondary. They will likely be aggressive at the trade deadline.
Riq Woolen should be there for the taking as the Eagles potentially tear everything down. He signed with them in March on a one-year contract, and given that he is still in his prime, it seems unlikely that he would re-sign with Philadelphia if they commit to a rebuild.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Brian Thomas Jr. to RaidersOf all the high-upside wide receivers that figure to be available at the deadline, none have a greater delta between their ceiling and floor than Brian Thomas Jr. His 1,282-yard, 10-touchdown rookie campaign displayed All-Pro potential, but in the two years since, he slipped behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the pecking order for targets in Jacksonville. The time for the Jaguars to move on from him is now, before his stock drops any further.The ideal fits for Thomas are either a team that would benefit from his price as he remains on a rookie contract or a team that would make him a long-term centerpiece if he rekindles his 2023 success. The Las Vegas Raiders fit the latter criteria. Their wide receiver depth is nonexistent, and there is no clear No. 1 weapon in the room. That needs to change by the time Fernando Mendoza takes over at quarterback, or else they risk stunting the top draft pick's early-career development. It still feels early in the Raiders' trajectory to begin buying, but after a surprisingly competitive first six weeks, it might already be time to spend.

        Opening night is here, and the fantasy basketball injury report is already crowded. Rookie Keaton Wagler is in line for a starting role with the Clippers, while Jaxson Hayes, Jalen Smith, Derrick Jones and Dennis Schroder could all see bigger workloads. Use this guide for the latest NBA injury news, expected return timelines, and the best waiver wire pickups, sleepers and streaming options to protect your fantasy basketball roster in 2026-27.Bradley Beal, Max Strus, Brandon Ingram ClippersBeal is listed as out, with knee inflammation and has no solid return date confirmed. Strus is dealing with a partial tear to his plantar fascia, an injury that will keep him out for at least the first couple of weeks of the season. Ingram was on track to carry a major offensive load when he was traded over from the Raptors late in the offseason. However, it was discovered that he had a partially torn Achilles, which has since been addressed through surgery, resulting in an uncertain return date for the 29-year-old. 
On the flip side, fifth-overall pick Keaton Wagler is projected to gain a significant boost and start at shooting guard. The handful of injuries to wing players puts the rookie in line for a great opportunity to get his NBA career off to a hot start. Additionally, Kris Dunn, Kobe Sanders and Gradey Dick are also likely to see more action while Beal and Strus remain sidelined. Derrick Jones will be the one to step up in the absence of Ingram. Jones has proven that he can provide good value as a starter and should serve as a reliable replacement. Jusuf Nurkic, Kyle Filipowski, Jazz Nurkic is expected to be sidelined until at least early November due to a partial plantar plate tear in his toe. Ace Bailey and Brice Sensabaugh could also see a boost by shifting to play some minutes at power forward.

De'Andre Hunter, Nique Clifford and Precious Achiuwa are all in place to take on more significant roles, as Simmons was initially expected to handle a heavy workload. The Kings are further shorthanded in the frontcourt, as both Raynaud (knee) and Cardwell (calf) are expected to miss a couple of weeks. Their absences open up a greater need for Achiuwa to step up, while new addition Jonathan Mogbo could also have a chance to make an impression. Mark Williams, SunsWilliams is expected to remain out for a few months as he recovers from surgery on a torn labrum in his shoulder. title: Dodgers 'fully expect' Shohei Ohtani to pitch in 2027, and they have three paths to take with two-way star - CBS Sports
description: The Dodgers say Ohtani will not need surgery after nursing two injuries in 2026, and they will have him return to
body:
The Dodgers say Ohtani will not need surgery after nursing two injuries in 2026, and they will have him return to double duty next year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Surgery is not on the table for Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani, who played through knee and biceps injuries late in the season and into the postseason, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman announced Wednesday. The Dodgers expect Ohtani to pitch next season and continue as a two-way player."That's not on the table," Friedman said when asked about Ohtani having surgery. "... I fully expect him to pitch next year. I not only expect him to pitch, we're excited about him pitching."  Ohtani, 32, did not pitch after July 3 due to the knee injury. He nursed the biceps injury throughout the season and it eventually contributed to the team's decision to shut him down as a pitcher. Ohtani threw bullpen sessions and faced hitters in live batting practice to prepare to return to the mound in late August, but he had to be shut down.The injuries clearly hampered Ohtani at the plate late in the year. He spent 15 days on the injured list in September, went 5 for 21 with eight strikeouts in five regular-season games after returning, then went 5 for 26 with 10 strikeouts in the postseason. Ohtani hit .167/.298/.240 with one home run in his final 26 games of 2026, postseason included.
Before the injuries, Ohtani made 14 starts and threw 85 ⅔ innings with a 1.79 ERA and terrific under-the-hood numbers. He has a career 2.83 ERA in 114 regular-season starts. Ohtani has pitched like an ace whenever he's been on the mound, so it's easy to understand why he and the Dodgers continue to pursue it.There are three paths the Dodgers can take with Ohtani as a pitcher in 2027.1. Let him pitch all yearMaintain the status quo, basically. Let Ohtani break camp as a regular member of the rotation and plan on pitching him every sixth day -- the Dodgers employ a full-time six-man rotation -- from Opening Day through the end of the season, which the Dodgers hope is at the end of the World Series. This is surely what Ohtani wants, and, of course, he has say in this matter.Here is the Dodgers rotation depth chart going into next season:RHP Shohei OhtaniRHP Yoshinobu YamamotoLHP Blake SnellRHP Tyler GlasnowRHP Roki SasakiLHP Justin WrobleskiRHP Emmet SheehanRHP Gavin Stone (coming off shoulder surgery)Even if the Dodgers are unable to re-sign Tarik Skubal, there is plenty of depth there to continue with the six-man rotation, and even skip Ohtani's starts now and then to give his body a break. Wrobleski and Sheehan are overqualified as No. 5-6 starters and Stone threw the ball quite well during his minor-league rehab appearances. Los Angeles could always sign a depth starter as well.

        
            
                Who's to blame for Dodgers' shocking NLCS loss vs. Brewers? Five places to point fingers
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
2. Start his season late (on the mound)Because Ohtani qualifies as a two-way player and thus counts against the roster as a position player, the Dodgers are still able to carry the full complement of 13 pitchers. They can slowly build Ohtani up as a pitcher during pregame work while he remains in the lineup as a hitter, then they can insert him into the rotation in, say, June. That could keep him healthiest in the long run.
This is more or less what the Dodgers did with Ohtani as he worked his way back from UCL surgery in 2025. He threw his bullpens and live batting practices in the afternoon, then hit at night. Ohtani made his first start on June 16 and gradually built up from one inning in June to six innings in September. Ohtani then made four starts and threw 20 ⅓ innings in the 2025 playoffs. There is proof of concept here. The Dodgers and Ohtani have done exactly this already.3. Use him as a relieverA fine idea that will be difficult to put into practice. Warming up in the bullpen (or even in the batting cage behind the dugout) would be difficult when Ohtani has to hit in the previous inning, or even if his lineup spot is due up fourth or fifth. Ohtani's lineup spot was eight spots away when he came out of the bullpen for Japan in the 2023 World Baseball Classic Championship Game.
Also, the Dodgers would lose the DH spot once Ohtani comes out of the game as a reliever. MLB's rules allow Ohtani to stay in the game as the DH when he's the starting pitcher, but not as the DH. The Dodgers could get around this by using him as the closer and as their final pitcher of the game. But again, how does he warm up? And if it goes to extra innings, you're down Ohtani's bat.The Dodgers should be good enough to win the NL West next season without a full season of Ohtani the pitcher, so starting him late seems like the best approach. That said, the difference between 15 starts of Ohtani and 23 starts of Ohtani could be the difference between getting a Wild Card Series bye or having to play in that best-of-three series. You want the bye, always.Ohtani just completed Year 3 of his landmark and heavily deferred 10-year, $700 million contract. The injuries and late-season fade at the plate make it nearly certain that Ohtani will not win a fourth consecutive MVP award, and the fifth MVP of his career.

title: College Football Playoff tiers: Miami, Georgia lead contenders at midseason - CBS Sports
description: Sorting the nation's playoff hopefuls into tiers based on résumés, ceilings and remaining paths as we enter the s
body:
Sorting the nation's playoff hopefuls into tiers based on résumés, ceilings and remaining paths as we enter the season's second half
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Validation.As the only CBS Sports voter to have Miami at No. 1 before the season, I'll admit, the Hurricanes climbed to the top spot in the AP poll a few weeks before I expected them to after midseason carnage across the top 25. Miami is one of only six unbeatens left on the board, and it doesn't appear that anyone's safe moving forward during a year of extreme parity in the sport.We're sifting through the AP Top 25 to separate elites from the teams still selling themselves on potential in Week 8. There's a handful of true contenders who have already shown a championship ceiling against quality competition, while others need a large sample size before belonging in that conversation.Reputation gets you attention, but play on the field and execution are what truly qualify in front of the CFP selection committee. Here's where the nation's playoff hopefuls fall in our contender tiers, with championship credentials driving the discussion.Tier A.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Georgia (6-1) The Bulldogs' stock price shouldn't change after their home loss to Auburn. Three turnovers from Gunner Stockton were to blame, and the likelihood that happens again this season is slim. Kirby Smart mentioned after the game that he felt Georgia beat itself, and it's hard to disagree with that. The Bulldogs remain our SEC favorite at midseason and should get to the CFP as a top-4 seed.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Miami (6-0) Survival. That's what it's about for the Hurricanes throughout the duration of the season. Getting past Notre Dame on Nov. 7 is not a necessity, but it would virtually secure a top-4 seed in the bracket and an opening-round bye if they do. We're sticking with the season-long projection that Miami will be the Power Four's lone unbeaten on Selection Sunday and enter the CFP as the No. 1 seed.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Notre Dame (6-1)Winning on the road is never easy. Doing it against a top-10 opponent is even more difficult. Notre Dame showed considerable fight at BYU after trailing 21-10 at halftime before taking a three-point lead in the fourth quarter prior to the Cougars' game-winning drive. The Fighting Irish are a better-executed goal-line play away from being unbeaten and ranked No. 1 in the AP poll, so it would be unwise to dismiss the Irish after one hiccup. That said, a loss to Miami in a couple of weeks severely alters Notre Dame's CFP outlook.
        
            
                Is Notre Dame in danger of missing CFP? Familiar conversation around Irish emerges after first loss of season
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Tier B.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    BYU (6-0) The best of the three unbeatens left in the Big 12, the Cougars catapulted themselves into the spotlight with the win over Notre Dame. Controversial ending aside, BYU earned it against a top-10 opponent with a victory that almost looked personal for Bear Bachmeier and his teammates. Can the Cougars bring that same level of swagger to UCF this weekend as a 6.5-point favorite or during their trip to Utah on Nov. 7? Those are two potential trouble spots for Kalani Sitake's squad.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Indiana (6-1)I wonder how often Curt Cignetti smirks when he reads that this Indiana team isn't as good as his last one. Well, duh. It's hard to replicate a 16-0, record-setting season when you replace a Heisman-winning quarterback and several other top-end playmakers. However, through seven games, the Hoosiers are literally a foot from being unbeaten on a 23-game winning streak entering Saturday's tilt at Michigan. There's still a lot to like about an elite-coached squad that's going to be a tough out in December. Despite the loss to Ohio State, I'm slotting Indiana above the Buckeyes at this point given the injury to Julian Sayin.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kentucky (6-1) Graced with an intellectual at quarterback and a first-year coach who might be the most confident leader in the FBS not named Curt Cignetti, the Wildcats are legit. There were doubts when this team trailed 17-0 at South Carolina and more when they lined up for the win against LSU the following week in overtime, but Will Stein delivers, man. Saturday's victory at Oklahoma might've been this squad's best given the setup -- a road underdog against a team coming off a rivalry victory over Texas in Red River. And Kentucky came through.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ohio State (6-1) The Buckeyes aren't in that top group because of Sayin's injury, a considerable unknown moving forward this season. It's up to backup Luke Fahey to keep Ohio State on track in the Big Ten picture and CFP conversation, with matchups left to play against USC, Oregon and Northwestern, among others. When you're equipped with Jeremiah Smith and an elite defense, you always have a chance, but the Buckeyes have been downgraded without QB1.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ole Miss (5-1) Pete Golding got his team's attention during their bye week earlier this month after a loss in Gainesville muddied up the hot start and revealed warts. Ole Miss has looked light years better defensively over the last two weekends, culminating with the Rebels' 28-point swat of Missouri in Week 7. They're a betting underdog Saturday at Texas, still have to play fifth-ranked Georgia and travel to Oklahoma before the Egg Bowl. Trinidad Chambliss, after what he showed during last season's CFP, is a warrior and gives Ole Miss a chance to win every game the rest of the season.Tier C.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Alabama (5-2) Outside of Texas, no team's stock has tanked faster than Alabama's over the last two games. Alabama hasn't scored a second-half point since Oct. 3 when the Crimson Tide humiliated Mississippi State, 56-23. Since then, the offense has been kept in check by Georgia and Tennessee, leading to jeers for Kalen DeBoer and Ryan Grubb. The upcoming showdown at LSU next month could determine the SEC's final at-large CFP entry.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LSU (5-2) Lane Kiffin's team hasn't exhausted their CFP chances just yet, and they could make a Miami-like impact as a high seed if they get there. The Tigers don't need another reminder of their ceiling. They need to start living there and playing with a better sense of urgency. The overtime loss at Kentucky still stings. However, win the games ahead -- especially Alabama -- and CFP seeding takes care of itself. This defense changes considerably without Princewill Umanmielen, so his return is vital.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tennessee (6-1) Jim Knowles is earning every penny of his $2 million salary as the Vols' defensive coordinator. He has fixed just about every problem that Josh Heupel asked of him, and Tennessee has a chance to win the SEC as a result. Last weekend's performance against Alabama was one of the most notable defensive game plans across the sport this fall as the Vols harassed Keelon Russell throughout. Independent of quarterback questions right now, Tennessee has the defense and run game with DeSean Bishop to make a run.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Texas Tech (6-0) Multiple Big 12 teams may appear in this season's CFP, but are any of the three frontrunners in the conference capable of winning a national championship? The Red Raiders got a first-place vote in the Week 8 AP poll following their destruction of Arizona State and only face one more ranked opponent -- Arizona -- down the stretch. Like last season, Texas Tech will be largely untested when the CFP begins unless it wins a conference title in December against a top-10 foe.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    UCLA (6-0)Defense wins championships, and this unit is humming in Los Angeles. Bob Chesney has flexed his coaching chops in Year 1 with the Bruins, instituting his own version of murder ball at the line of scrimmage. There's nothing sexy about UCLA -- it just keeps winning and taking advantage of one of the Big Ten's most favorable slates. The victory at Oregon was meaningful, but the rivalry finale against USC is the showdown that will be season-defining.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Utah (6-0) Morgan Scalley knows it's easier to overlook issues after wins, but you can bet the Utes' coaching staff will work tirelessly this week to correct the mistakes suffered during last week's win at Colorado. That same performance against Houston on Saturday, two weeks from now against BYU or even at Arizona in November, would crash the season.Tier D.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Florida (5-2) The Gators got a big win at Texas last week, but Florida still has problems. Defensively, the Gators have been a mess in SEC play. Jon Sumrall continues to harp on the challenges of building a program and the inconsistencies that are bound to persist. At least he knows Florida has two quarterbacks capable of winning games against quality opponents. If they could get the failure-to-show against South Carolina back, the Gators' national outlook would be much different.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Houston (6-1) Conner Weigman has thrown 20 touchdowns this season and accounted for five total scores during last week's win against Oklahoma State. The Cougars can score in a hurry, and their only loss was a disputed failed two-point conversion at Texas Tech in September. This team's dangerous and gets Utah this weekend.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Iowa (5-1) Ten wins might not be enough to reach the CFP as an at-large selection given this strength of schedule, so the Hawkeyes need to run the table from here. The only ranked opponent left is Northwestern on the road come Nov. 7, so it's possible. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Missouri (5-2) Scoring only three points at Ole Miss is really unexplainable when you consider the Tigers were coming off consecutive 200-yard performances from Jamal Roberts on the ground, with quarterback play from Austin Simmons that trounced most others inside the top 25. It felt like the air got let out of the balloon in Oxford, and it's unclear if Missouri can get it back.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Texas (4-2) There's no excuse for what's going down on the Forty Acres. From No. 1 to almost outside the top 20 over the last two games, offensive struggles continue to damage the Longhorns' title chances under Steve Sarkisian. He can't get it figured out with Arch Manning, it seems. There's no dominant rushing attack despite offseason acquisitions, and now, the Longhorns must battle Ole Miss and potentially others over the next few games without their top defensive player. The roster is handsomely paid and talented, but the coaching isn't good enough here across the board to win it all.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    USC (6-1) The conversation changes if the Trojans beat Ohio State in Week 8, but for now, there's no convincing anyone that Lincoln Riley can beat a quality opponent in the Big Ten until he actually does it. Given Oregon's struggles, USC has to look back at that home loss as a missed opportunity given the talent on this year's team.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Wake Forest (6-1) Bob Chesney and Will Stein are crowding the coach-of-the-year buzz and rightfully so, but what Jake Dickert has done with a ragtag roster in the ACC is truly impressive. Wake Forest has spent considerably less money on its roster compared to UCLA and Kentucky, but is on a tear since its only loss of the season -- a 33-20 setback to Miami back on Sept. 18. If the Demon Deacons beat SMU in Dallas in November, they're heading toward an 11-1 finish and a berth in the ACC title game. Who saw that coming?
